title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation, Known Issues & QBR Playbook
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview
========
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard approach for enterprise customer onboarding with a focus on integration, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, and the recurring health check / QBR cadence. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and on-call SRE teams partnering with enterprise customers during the first 90-180 days of production adoption.

Objectives
- Reduce time-to-value by providing a predictable technical onboarding and integration checklist.
- Minimize customer-impacting issues via clear escalation paths and ownership.
- Provide repeatable templates for health checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs).
- Capture and circulate known issues & mitigations to avoid repeat incidents.

Scope and applicability
- Applies to paid enterprise customers adopting Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers technical integration, config/permissions, performance validation, SLO alignment, escalation, and QBR preparation.
- Not intended for self-serve free-tier customers; use the Quickstart templates in eng-developer-experience for those cases.

Owner and contributors
- Document owner: Customer Success (primary)
- Day-to-day maintainers: SE Integration squad, Support Ops
- Reviewers: Product (API & Platform), Eng-SRE, Security

Key roles and responsibilities
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): overall onboarding coordinator, commercial touchpoints, QBR owner.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical lead on integration, runbook handover, acceptance criteria.
- Support (L1/L2): triage for incidents, maintain knowledge base entries.
- Eng-SRE (L3): on-call escalation for platform issues (SLO breaches, infra incidents).
- Customer technical lead: provides access, participates in joint tests, and signs off on handover.

Onboarding phases (90-day recommended cadence)
1) Discovery (Day 0-7)
   - Kickoff meeting: agenda, stakeholders, success metrics, and timeline.
   - Deliverables: Access matrix, initial data residency and compliance constraints, list of core use cases.
2) Integration (Day 7-30)
   - API key provisioning and environment setup (staging, prod).
   - Network & security: IP allowlists, VPC peering/VPN (for Private deployments), KMS/HSM integration checklist.
   - Feature enablement: streaming, function calls, embeddings, model pinning.
   - Run smoke tests and validation suite.
3) Performance validation (Day 30-60)
   - Baseline throughput and p50/p95 latency using customer workload.
   - Apply recommended batching, caching, and quantization profiles from Redwood Optimize.
   - Acceptance criteria: latency within agreed SLOs, error rate < agreed threshold, cost per token in expected band.
4) Handover & go-live (Day 60-90)
   - Handover doc delivered: runbooks, alert contacts, escalation matrix, rollback plan.
   - Final go/no-go checklist and sign-off by CSM, SE, and customer technical lead.
   - Schedule first 30/60/90-day health checks and QBR cadence.

Integration checklist (technical)
- Accounts & access
  - Create API key(s) with least-privilege scopes.
  - Assign RBAC roles for devs, ops, and monitoring.
- Networking & security
  - Confirm allowlist IPs or configure VPC peering / Private deployment network.
  - Validate TLS and certificate chains for private control plane.
  - Validate KMS integration and key rotation policy.
- Configuration & feature flags
  - Pin model versions and rollout policies in config.
  - Set batching and cache TTLs per workload profile.
- Observability & tracing
  - Integrate tracing hooks and propagate request IDs.
  - Configure per-route dashboards in Redwood Console and grant customer read access where appropriate.
- Tests to run
  - Auth smoke tests: successful token auth and expected 403/401 behavior.
  - Functional tests: basic generation/chat/embedding calls, function calling paths.
  - Load tests: burst and sustained throughput at expected QPS (do not exceed dedicated capacity without coordination).

Escalation matrix (technical & support)
- Tier 0 (Customer level): CSM initial report, standard Support Portal ticket
- Tier 1 (Support L1): Triage within 2 business hours, attempt known-workarounds from KB
- Tier 2 (Support L2 / SE): Detailed troubleshooting, logs collection, reproduce steps (SLA: 4 business hours for high-severity)
- Tier 3 (Eng-SRE / Product): Deep debugging, rollout of emergency patches, infra changes (SLA: 8 business hours for critical in-production incidents)

Escalation contact table
- CSM: <CSM name/email> (owner for customer comms)
- Support Pager: support-oncall@redwood.ai (24x7 triage)
- Eng-SRE Pager: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai (for platform incidents)
- SE Integration: se-integration@redwood.ai (business hours)

Severity definitions and expected response
- Sev 1 (Production outage): system unavailable for customer primary traffic or major SLA breach. Initial response: 15 minutes. Updates: every 30 minutes until mitigated.
- Sev 2 (Degraded service): Major feature degraded, significant errors or latency increase. Initial response: 1 hour. Updates: hourly.
- Sev 3 (Minor issue): Non-critical functionality; degraded but acceptable. Initial response: 1 business day.

Known issues and workarounds (living section)
- Issue: Occasional 502s for long-streaming sessions when routing through proxy layer.
  - Symptoms: streaming disconnect at ~60-90s, partial tokens returned.
  - Temporary workaround: Re-try with exponential backoff and reduced chunk sizes; enable direct route to streaming-optimized model variant if customer is on Dedicated.
  - Owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime, KB entry ID: KB-2026-042
- Issue: Higher than expected p95 latency for short prompts with large context windows.
  - Symptoms: p95 spikes during mixed short/long prompt traffic.
  - Workaround: Apply per-route batching config to separate short prompt traffic; pin a smaller context-length optimized model.
  - Owner: SE Integration, KB entry ID: KB-2026-057
- Issue: Private deployment onboarding delays due to internal firewall rules.
  - Symptoms: Control plane fails to reach customer agent; installs hang at step 3.
  - Workaround: Provide explicit firewall rule template (see Appendix A) and remote troubleshooting session.
  - Owner: Eng-Private-Deployments, KB entry ID: KB-2026-061

Support process and handoffs
- Ticketing: All issues must be logged in Support Portal with customer ID, impact, and reproducible steps.
- SLAs: Response and escalation must follow the severity matrix above.
- KB updates: For any recurring issue, create or update a KB article with reproduction, mitigation, and permanent fix ETA.
- RCA & postmortem: For Sev 1 outages, Eng-SRE owns the postmortem within 72 hours; CSM coordinates customer-facing summary and follow-up actions.

Health checks and QBR materials
- 30-day health check (template):
  - Summary of integration status and outstanding items.
  - Usage and cost snapshot (tokens, embeddings, avg latency).
  - Error-rate summary, top 3 errors and mitigations.
  - Next actions and owners.
- 60/90-day health check: deeper performance tuning review; present Redwood Optimize recommendations and cost-savings opportunities.
- QBR cadence: Quarterly by default for enterprise customers; agenda: usage trends, performance vs SLOs, roadmap alignment, risk review.
- QBR deliverables: Slide deck (template below), action items with owners, and updated success metrics.

QBR slide deck template (recommended sections)
1) Executive summary: adoption highlights and top KPI changes
2) Reliability & performance: SLO attainment (p50/p95 latency, error rate), incident summary
3) Cost and efficiency: tokens consumed, per-call unit economics, Optimize suggestions implemented
4) Product roadmap alignment: upcoming features relevant to customer
5) Risks & mitigation: security/compliance items or capacity constraints
6) Action items & next steps

Acceptance criteria and sign-off checklist (Go-Live)
- Functional: All smoke tests pass in prod environment.
- Security: KMS and RBAC validated; penetration test (if required) scheduled.
- Performance: Latency and error-rate within agreed thresholds for 7-day rolling window.
- Observability: Dashboards and alerts configured and tested.
- Business: Commercial contract and billing configured.
- Sign-off: CSM, SE, Eng-SRE, and customer technical lead.

Appendices
A) Firewall / network template (example rules)
- Allow egress to control-plane.redwood.ai:443
- Allow inbound only from engineered customer CIDR for webhooks (if used)
- Allow NTP/DNS as required by customer infra

B) KB & runbook references
- KB-2026-042: Streaming disconnect workarounds
- KB-2026-057: Mixed traffic latency mitigations
- KB-2026-061: Private deployment firewall checklist
- Runbook: eng-platform/deployment-rollback-v1

Maintenance and document governance
- Review cadence: This playbook is reviewed quarterly by CS and SE leads.
- Change log: Record major edits and the reason in the embedded changelog section (below).

Changelog
- 2026-03-25: Created (Ava Chen)
- 2026-03-30: Added Known Issues section and Escalation contact details (Liam Patel, Sofia Martinez)

If you are executing an onboarding that differs from this template (for example, multi-region Dedicated deployments or fully air-gapped Private installs), contact eng-private-deployments@redwood.ai to request the specialized checklist.

Templates and attachments
